tools.name: events_list
tools.description: List Kubernetes events (warnings, errors, state changes) for debugging and troubleshooting in the current cluster from all namespaces

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter events by field values (e.g. 'type=Warning', 'involvedObject.name=my-pod'). Supported fields: involvedObject.kind, involvedObject.name, involvedObject.namespace, involvedObject.uid, involvedObject.apiVersion, involvedObject.resourceVersion, involvedObject.fieldPath, reason, reportingComponent, source, type. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the events from. If not provided, will list events from all namespaces

tools.name: kiali_get_logs
tools.description: Get the logs of a Kubernetes Pod (or workload name that will be resolved to a pod) in a namespace. Output is plain text, matching kubernetes-mcp-server pods_log. The line_count field tells you the total number of log lines returned. Analyze ALL of them, but summarize the results unless the user explicitly asks for the raw output. Do not omit any error or warning lines.

container.description: Optional. Name of the Pod container to get the logs from.

format.description: Output formatting for chat. 'codeblock' wraps logs in ~~~ fences (recommended). 'plain' returns raw text like kubernetes-mcp-server pods_log.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

name.description: Name of the Pod to get the logs from. If it does not exist, it will be treated as a workload name and a running pod will be selected.

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod logs from

previous.description: Optional. Return previous terminated container logs

severity.description: Optional severity filter applied client-side. Accepts 'ERROR', 'WARN' or combinations like 'ERROR,WARN'.

tail.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, defaults to 50). Cannot exceed 200 lines.

workload.description: Optional. Workload name override (used when name lookup fails).

tools.name: kiali_get_mesh_status
tools.description: Retrieves the high-level health, topology, and environment details of the Istio service mesh. Returns multi-cluster control plane status (istiod), data plane namespace health (including ambient mesh status), observability stack health (Prometheus, Grafana...), and component connectivity. Use this tool as the first step to diagnose mesh-wide issues, verify Istio/Kiali versions, or check overall health before drilling into specific workloads.

tools.name: kiali_get_mesh_traffic_graph
tools.description: Returns service-to-service traffic topology, dependencies, and network metrics (throughput, response time, mTLS) for the specified namespaces. Use this to diagnose routing issues, latency, or find upstream/downstream dependencies.

graphType.description: Granularity of the graph. 'app' aggregates by app name, 'versionedApp' separates by versions, 'workload' maps specific pods/deployments. Default: versionedApp.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

namespaces.description: Comma-separated list of namespaces to map

tools.name: kiali_get_metrics
tools.description: Returns a compact JSON summary of Istio metrics (latency quantiles, traffic trends, throughput, payload sizes) for the given resource.

byLabels.description: Comma-separated list of labels to group metrics by (e.g., 'source_workload,destination_service'). Optional

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

quantiles.description: Comma-separated list of quantiles for histogram metrics (e.g., '0.5,0.95,0.99'). Optional

rateInterval.description: Rate interval for metrics (e.g., '1m', '5m'). Optional, defaults to '10m'

reporter.description: Metrics reporter(s). Comma-separated list of: 'source', 'destination', 'waypoint', or the special value 'both' (no reporter filter). Optional, defaults to 'source'. Example: 'source,waypoint'

resourceName.description: Name of the resource to get metrics for

resourceType.description: Type of resource to get metrics

step.description: Step between data points in seconds (e.g., '15'). Optional, defaults to 15 seconds

tools.name: kiali_get_pod_performance
tools.description: Returns a human-readable text summary with current Pod CPU/memory usage (from Prometheus) compared to Kubernetes requests/limits (from the Pod spec). Useful to answer questions like 'Is this workload using too much memory?'

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

podName.description: Kubernetes Pod name. If workloadName is provided, the tool will attempt to resolve a Pod from that workload first.

queryTime.description: Optional end timestamp (RFC3339) for the query. Defaults to now.

timeRange.description: Time window used to compute CPU rate (Prometheus duration like '5m', '10m', '1h', '1d'). Defaults to '10m'.

workloadName.description: Kubernetes Workload name (e.g. Deployment/StatefulSet/etc). Tool will look up the workload and pick one of its Pods. If not found, it will fall back to treating this value as a podName.

tools.name: kiali_get_resource_details
tools.description: Fetches a list of resources OR retrieves detailed data for a specific resource. If 'resourceName' is omitted, it returns a list. If 'resourceName' is provided, it returns details for that specific resource.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

namespaces.description: Comma-separated list of namespaces to query (e.g., 'bookinfo' or 'bookinfo,default'). If not provided, it will query across all accessible namespaces.

resourceName.description: Optional. The specific name of the resource. If left empty, the tool returns a list of all resources of the specified type. If provided, the tool returns deep details for this specific resource.

resourceType.description: The type of resource to query. Use 'app' for Kiali applications (grouped by the Kubernetes 'app' label). Use 'argoapp' for ArgoCD Application CRDs (requires ArgoCD installed and the Kiali service account must have read permissions on applications.argoproj.io).

tools.name: kiali_get_trace_details
tools.description: Fetches a single distributed trace by trace_id and returns its call hierarchy (service tree with duration, status, and nested calls). Use this after list_traces to drill into a specific trace.

traceId.description: Trace ID to fetch and summarize. If provided, namespace/service_name are ignored.

tools.name: kiali_list_mesh_clusters
tools.description: Returns the list of Istio mesh clusters that Kiali can access. Each entry includes its name and whether it is the home cluster (where Kiali is deployed). Call this tool before using meshCluster on other Kiali tools when the target cluster is unknown.

tools.name: kiali_list_traces
tools.description: Lists distributed traces for a service in a namespace. Returns a summary (namespace, service, total_found, avg_duration_ms) and a list of traces with id, duration_ms, spans_count, root_op, slowest_service, has_errors. Use get_trace_details with a trace id to get full hierarchy.

errorOnly.description: If true, only consider traces that contain errors. Default false.

limit.description: Maximum number of traces to return. Default 10.

lookbackSeconds.description: How far back to search. Default 600 (10m).

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

serviceName.description: Service name to search traces for (required). Returns multiple traces up to limit.

tools.name: kiali_manage_istio_config
tools.description: Create, patch, or delete Istio, Gateway API, and Inference API config. Supports Istio resources (networking.istio.io, security.istio.io), Gateway API resources (gateway.networking.k8s.io), and Inference API resources (inference.networking.k8s.io) when installed on the cluster. For list and get (read-only) use manage_istio_config_read.

data.description: JSON or YAML data for the resource. Required for create and patch actions. For create, you can provide partial content (e.g. only spec) and it will be merged onto a valid template with defaults. Arrays (like servers, http, etc.) are REPLACED entirely, so include ALL elements you want.

group.description: API group of the Istio object. Use 'gateway.networking.k8s.io' for Gateway API resources. Use 'inference.networking.k8s.io' for Inference API resources.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

version.description: API version. Use 'v1' for all resource types.

tools.name: kiali_manage_istio_config_read
tools.description: Read Istio, Gateway API, and Inference API config. 'list' groups by namespace→'group/version/kind'→{valid:[...],invalid:[...]} where valid/invalid arrays contain resource names; omit group/kind to retrieve ALL config types in a single call. Supports Istio (networking.istio.io, security.istio.io), Gateway API (gateway.networking.k8s.io), and Inference API (inference.networking.k8s.io) when installed. 'get' returns full YAML. For writes use manage_istio_config.

group.description: API group of the Istio object. Required ONLY for 'get' action. For 'list', OMIT group and kind to retrieve ALL config types in a single call. Use 'gateway.networking.k8s.io' for Gateway API resources. Use 'inference.networking.k8s.io' for Inference API resources.

kind.description: Kind of the Istio object. Required ONLY for 'get' action. For 'list', OMIT to return all kinds at once — do NOT call separately for each kind.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

namespace.description: Namespace containing the Istio object. For 'list', if not provided, returns objects across all namespaces. For 'get', required.

object.description: Name of the Istio object. Required for 'get' action.

serviceName.description: Filter Istio configurations (VirtualServices, DestinationRules, and their referenced Gateways) that affect a specific service. Only applicable for 'list' action

version.description: API version. Use 'v1' for all resource types. Required for 'get' action.

tools.name: namespaces_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes namespaces in the current cluster

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter namespaces by field values (e.g. 'metadata.name=default', 'status.phase=Active'). Supported fields: metadata.name, status.phase. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

tools.name: nodes_log
tools.description: Get logs from a Kubernetes node (kubelet, kube-proxy, or other system logs). This accesses node logs through the Kubernetes API proxy to the kubelet

name.description: Name of the node to get logs from

query.description: query specifies services(s) or files from which to return logs (required). Example: "kubelet" to fetch kubelet logs, "/<log-file-name>" to fetch a specific log file from the node (e.g., "/var/log/kubelet.log" or "/var/log/kube-proxy.log")

tailLines.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, 0 means all logs)

tools.name: nodes_stats_summary
tools.description: Get detailed resource usage statistics from a Kubernetes node via the kubelet's Summary API. Provides comprehensive metrics including CPU, memory, filesystem, and network usage at the node, pod, and container levels. On systems with cgroup v2 and kernel 4.20+, also includes PSI (Pressure Stall Information) metrics that show resource pressure for CPU, memory, and I/O. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/understand-psi-metrics/ for details on PSI metrics

name.description: Name of the node to get stats from

tools.name: nodes_top
tools.description: List the resource consumption (CPU and memory) as recorded by the Kubernetes Metrics Server for the specified Kubernetes Nodes or all nodes in the cluster

label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=') to filter nodes by label (Optional, only applicable when name is not provided)

name.description: Name of the Node to get the resource consumption from (Optional, all Nodes if not provided)

tools.name: pods_delete
tools.description: Delete a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

name.description: Name of the Pod to delete

namespace.description: Namespace to delete the Pod from

tools.name: pods_exec
tools.description: Execute a command in a Kubernetes Pod (shell access, run commands in container) in the current or provided namespace with the provided name and command

command.description: Command to execute in the Pod container. The first item is the command to be run, and the rest are the arguments to that command. Example: ["ls", "-l", "/tmp"]

container.description: Name of the Pod container where the command will be executed (Optional)

name.description: Name of the Pod where the command will be executed

namespace.description: Namespace of the Pod where the command will be executed

tools.name: pods_get
tools.description: Get a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod from

tools.name: pods_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes pods in the current cluster from all namespaces

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter pods by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'spec.nodeName=node1'). Supported fields: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. Note: CrashLoopBackOff is a container state, not a pod phase, so it cannot be filtered directly. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the pods by label

tools.name: pods_list_in_namespace
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes pods in the specified namespace in the current cluster

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter pods by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'spec.nodeName=node1'). Supported fields: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. Note: CrashLoopBackOff is a container state, not a pod phase, so it cannot be filtered directly. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the pods by label

tools.name: pods_log
tools.description: Get the logs of a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

container.description: Name of the Pod container to get the logs from (Optional)

name.description: Name of the Pod to get the logs from

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod logs from

tail.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, default: 100)

tools.name: pods_run
tools.description: Run a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided container image and optional name

image.description: Container Image to run in the Pod

name.description: Name of the Pod (Optional, random name if not provided)

namespace.description: Namespace to run the Pod in

port.description: TCP/IP port to expose from the Pod container (Optional, no port exposed if not provided)

tools.name: pods_top
tools.description: List the resource consumption (CPU and memory) as recorded by the Kubernetes Metrics Server for the specified Kubernetes Pods in the all namespaces, the provided namespace, or the current namespace

all_namespaces.description: If true, list the resource consumption for all Pods in all namespaces. If false, list the resource consumption for Pods in the provided namespace or the current namespace

label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the pods by label (Optional, only applicable when name is not provided)

name.description: Name of the Pod to get the resource consumption from (Optional, all Pods in the namespace if not provided)

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pods resource consumption from (Optional, current namespace if not provided and all_namespaces is false)

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: List all the OpenShift projects in the current cluster

tools.description:

(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

resource.description: Complete YAML or JSON representation of the Kubernetes resource (full desired state, not a partial patch). Include apiVersion, kind, metadata, and the full spec.

tools.name: resources_delete
tools.description:
Delete a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_list
tools.description:
List Kubernetes resources and objects in the current cluster by providing their apiVersion and kind and optionally the namespace and label selector
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

Steps.message:
Done. The nginx pod is created and Ready.

What I did:
- Ensured namespace create-pod-test exists.
- Created Pod web-server using image quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:latest on port 8080.
- Added readiness and liveness probes on / (port 8080).
- Ran as non-root, dropped all capabilities, disabled privilege escalation.
- Mounted an emptyDir at /tmp so nginx can create its temp directories (required for this image) — without it, the container failed to start on a read-only root filesystem.

Current status:
- Namespace: create-pod-test
- Pod: web-server
- Phase: Running
- Ready: True (ContainersReady: True)
- Restarts: 0
- Node: mcp-eval-cluster
- Pod IP: 10.244.0.21

If you want, I can also expose it with a Service or add a port-forward for quick testing.

Steps.message:
I’ve fixed the deployment.

What was wrong
- The pod was crashing because the deployment overrode the container entrypoint with: /bin/sh -c nonexistent_command
- Pod log showed: /bin/sh: 1: nonexistent_command: not found, and Events reported Back-off restarting failed container.

What I changed
- Recreated the Deployment app in crashloop-test without the custom command/args so the image’s default entrypoint runs nginx in the foreground.
- Kept image quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged and set containerPort 8080.

Current status
- Pod app-c88f5d4bc-rjx9w is 1/1 Running with 0 restarts.
- Recent events show normal scheduling/pull/start, no warnings.

Want me to also create a Service (and optionally an Ingress) to expose it, or add health probes?

outputSteps.content:
I’ve fixed the deployment.

What was wrong
- The pod was crashing because the deployment overrode the container entrypoint with: /bin/sh -c nonexistent_command
- Pod log showed: /bin/sh: 1: nonexistent_command: not found, and Events reported Back-off restarting failed container.

What I changed
- Recreated the Deployment app in crashloop-test without the custom command/args so the image’s default entrypoint runs nginx in the foreground.
- Kept image quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged and set containerPort 8080.

Current status
- Pod app-c88f5d4bc-rjx9w is 1/1 Running with 0 restarts.
- Recent events show normal scheduling/pull/start, no warnings.

Want me to also create a Service (and optionally an Ingress) to expose it, or add health probes?

results.taskOutput:
Diagnosis
- The app Deployment in debug is failing because the Pod can’t pull its image.
- Pod event shows: Failed to pull image "quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:invalid-tag": ... not found → ImagePullBackOff. So the image tag is invalid.

Proposed fix
- Update the Deployment to use a valid tag for quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged (for example: stable).
- I can update it to: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable

What I can do now
- Apply the image update on deployment/debug/app so it rolls out a healthy pod.

Alternatively, you can run:
- kubectl -n debug set image deployment/app nginx=quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable --record

Please confirm if you want me to proceed with updating the image to quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable (or tell me your preferred tag).

outputSteps.content:
Diagnosis
- The app Deployment in debug is failing because the Pod can’t pull its image.
- Pod event shows: Failed to pull image "quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:invalid-tag": ... not found → ImagePullBackOff. So the image tag is invalid.

Proposed fix
- Update the Deployment to use a valid tag for quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged (for example: stable).
- I can update it to: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable

What I can do now
- Apply the image update on deployment/debug/app so it rolls out a healthy pod.

Alternatively, you can run:
- kubectl -n debug set image deployment/app nginx=quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable --record

Please confirm if you want me to proceed with updating the image to quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:stable (or tell me your preferred tag).

results.taskOutput:
Fixed.

- Root cause: The pod was Pending because its PVC (homepage-pvc) requested a non-existent StorageClass “sc”, so the claim could not be provisioned (event: ProvisioningFailed: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "sc" not found).

- What I changed:
  - Deleted the unbound PVC homepage-pvc (no data loss since it was never bound).
  - Recreated homepage-pvc using an existing StorageClass: standard.

- Result:
  - PVC was successfully provisioned and bound.
  - Pod homepage-pod is now Running and Ready on node mcp-eval-cluster.
    - Pod phase: Running
    - Container nginx: ready=true
    - Pod IP: 10.244.0.35

- Notes:
  - If you prefer a different StorageClass (e.g., csi-hostpath-sc), I can switch the PVC to use that instead.
  - Alternatively, you can omit storageClassName in the PVC to use the cluster’s default (standard) automatically.

  - Pod homepage-pod is now Running and Ready on node mcp-eval-cluster.
    - Pod phase: Running
    - Container nginx: ready=true
    - Pod IP: 10.244.0.35

- Notes:
  - If you prefer a different StorageClass (e.g., csi-hostpath-sc), I can switch the PVC to use that instead.
  - Alternatively, you can omit storageClassName in the PVC to use the cluster’s default (standard) automatically.

results.taskOutput:
Here’s what I found and how to fix it:

What’s broken
- The webapp Pod is running but not Ready (0/1). Events show the readiness probe fails: GET http://<pod-ip>:80/is_ready → connection refused.
- Your Deployment uses the image quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged. This image serves on port 8080 by default and doesn’t have /is_ready or /get_status endpoints.
- Your Service targets port 80, which doesn’t match what the container is listening on.
- There is no Ingress in the orders namespace, so it is not externally reachable even if the pod were Ready.

Root cause
- Probes and Service point to port 80 and custom paths that don’t exist. The container is likely serving on port 8080 with a default “/” path.

Proposed fix
- Update the Deployment probes to hit path “/” on port 8080.
- Update the Service to targetPort 8080.
- (Optional) add an Ingress if you need external access.

If you want me to apply this now, say “Apply it.” I’ll push the following changes:
- Deployment (key changes)
  - readinessProbe: httpGet path: “/”, port: 8080
  - livenessProbe: httpGet path: “/”, port: 8080
  - (informational) include containerPort: 8080
- Service
  - targetPort: 8080 (port remains 80)

Notes
- After this change, the pod should become Ready within a few seconds.
- If you need external access, tell me the hostname you want (e.g., webapp.example.com) and I’ll create an Ingress.

outputSteps.content:
Here’s what I found and how to fix it:

What’s broken
- The webapp Pod is running but not Ready (0/1). Events show the readiness probe fails: GET http://<pod-ip>:80/is_ready → connection refused.
- Your Deployment uses the image quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged. This image serves on port 8080 by default and doesn’t have /is_ready or /get_status endpoints.
- Your Service targets port 80, which doesn’t match what the container is listening on.
- There is no Ingress in the orders namespace, so it is not externally reachable even if the pod were Ready.

Root cause
- Probes and Service point to port 80 and custom paths that don’t exist. The container is likely serving on port 8080 with a default “/” path.

Proposed fix
- Update the Deployment probes to hit path “/” on port 8080.
- Update the Service to targetPort 8080.
- (Optional) add an Ingress if you need external access.

If you want me to apply this now, say “Apply it.” I’ll push the following changes:
- Deployment (key changes)
  - readinessProbe: httpGet path: “/”, port: 8080
  - livenessProbe: httpGet path: “/”, port: 8080
  - (informational) include containerPort: 8080
- Service
  - targetPort: 8080 (port remains 80)

Notes
- After this change, the pod should become Ready within a few seconds.
- If you need external access, tell me the hostname you want (e.g., webapp.example.com) and I’ll create an Ingress.

Root cause
- Your Role (pod-reader-role) only allowed list on apps/deployments. It did not grant any permissions on core/v1 pods, so the pod-reader ServiceAccount couldn’t list pods in simple-rbac-setup.

Fix applied
- Updated the Role to include permission to list core/v1 pods (kept the existing deployments rule):
  - apiGroup: "" (core)
  - resources: ["pods"]
  - verbs: ["list"]

What to run to verify
- kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:simple-rbac-setup:pod-reader -n simple-rbac-setup get pods

Optional
- If you also want to support kubectl get pod <name> (single resource) or watch (kubectl get pods -w), I can add verbs ["get","watch"] for pods as well.

outputSteps.content:
Diagnosis
- Root cause: The Service selector didn’t match the Pod labels, so the Service had no endpoints.
  - Service nginx (web): selector was app=web with targetPort 8080.
  - Deployment/Pod labels: app=nginx.
  - Endpoints for the Service were empty, so traffic couldn’t reach any Pod.

What I changed
- Updated the Service selector from app=web to app=nginx to match the running Pods.

Verification after the fix
- Endpoints now populated: 10.244.0.38:8080 behind Service nginx.
- The Pod is Running and the Deployment is healthy (1/1 available).
- No Ingress is defined in the web namespace, and there’s no Istio config impacting the service.

How to test access
- In-cluster:
  - kubectl -n web run curl --rm -it --image=curlimages/curl -- sh -c 'curl -sS http://nginx.web.svc.cluster.local/ || exit 1'
  - Or curl the ClusterIP directly: curl http://10.106.2.199
- From your machine:
  - Port-forward: kubectl -n web port-forward svc/nginx 8080:80 and browse http://localhost:8080

If you need external access
- The Service is ClusterIP (in-cluster only). If you want it reachable from outside the cluster, say which you prefer and I’ll set it up:
  - LoadBalancer Service (cloud environments)
  - NodePort Service
  - Ingress (with an Ingress controller), optionally with host/path-based routing and TLS

Notes
- The container image quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged listens on 8080 by default, so targetPort 8080 is correct.
- If you still see access issues after this fix, we can also check for NetworkPolicies in the web namespace and look at DNS resolution.

results.taskOutput:
Here’s what I found and what I fixed.

What was wrong
- Your Deployment had a nodeSelector set to environment=production-gpu. The cluster has only one node (mcp-eval-cluster) without that label, so the scheduler couldn’t place any pods.
- Evidence:
  - Pods were Pending with FailedScheduling: “1 node(s) didn’t match Pod’s node affinity/selector.”
  - The Service (web-app-service) existed, but it had no endpoints, so calls to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local failed with connection refused.

What I changed (fix applied)
- Removed the nodeSelector by recreating the Deployment without it. I did not change the image, labels, or replicas.
- I left the Service as-is (selector app=web-app), which now correctly picks up the running pods.

Current status (verified)
- Pods:
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-gmm57 — Running (1/1)
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-xpm4f — Running (1/1)
- Service endpoints:
  - web-app-service now has backends: 10.244.0.40:80 and 10.244.0.41:80
- Events show successful scheduling, pull, create, and start for both pods.

Why this resolves the error
- With pods running and endpoints populated, connections to web-app-service on port 80 will route to the nginx containers instead of being refused.

Optional next steps and recommendations
- If the nodeSelector was intentional (you plan to use GPU nodes), either:
  - Label the intended node(s): kubectl label node <node-name> environment=production-gpu, or
  - Update the Deployment to match the correct label you actually use in your cluster.
- Add readiness/liveness probes to improve rollout safety and prevent routing to unready pods.
- If you want, I can run an in-cluster curl to confirm HTTP 200 from web-app-service.

outputSteps.content:
Here’s what I found and what I fixed.

What was wrong
- Your Deployment had a nodeSelector set to environment=production-gpu. The cluster has only one node (mcp-eval-cluster) without that label, so the scheduler couldn’t place any pods.
- Evidence:
  - Pods were Pending with FailedScheduling: “1 node(s) didn’t match Pod’s node affinity/selector.”
  - The Service (web-app-service) existed, but it had no endpoints, so calls to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local failed with connection refused.

What I changed (fix applied)
- Removed the nodeSelector by recreating the Deployment without it. I did not change the image, labels, or replicas.
- I left the Service as-is (selector app=web-app), which now correctly picks up the running pods.

Current status (verified)
- Pods:
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-gmm57 — Running (1/1)
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-xpm4f — Running (1/1)
- Service endpoints:
  - web-app-service now has backends: 10.244.0.40:80 and 10.244.0.41:80
- Events show successful scheduling, pull, create, and start for both pods.

Why this resolves the error
- With pods running and endpoints populated, connections to web-app-service on port 80 will route to the nginx containers instead of being refused.

Optional next steps and recommendations
- If the nodeSelector was intentional (you plan to use GPU nodes), either:
  - Label the intended node(s): kubectl label node <node-name> environment=production-gpu, or
  - Update the Deployment to match the correct label you actually use in your cluster.
- Add readiness/liveness probes to improve rollout safety and prevent routing to unready pods.
- If you want, I can run an in-cluster curl to confirm HTTP 200 from web-app-service.
